pattern: Myth vs fact carousel built on the 'Why diets don't work / Žiadne zázračné diéty' hook seen across TikTok and Meta ads, remade around doctor-led care and the persona's objections
why: The 'tried every diet' pain stops busy professionals, and each myth answers one real objection (real doctor, travel, price, follow-up), so every swipe resolves a doubt.

slides.headline: Vyskúšali ste už všetky diéty a nič?
body: Možno vám nechýbala vôľa, ale lekár.

findings.message: Confirm the doctor in blur-doctor.jpg is unidentifiable or has given written consent; otherwise remove the face or add a clear dramatization label.
Check with the operator that the questionnaire time and the cancel-anytime terms are accurate, since operational claims must be true.

slides.issues: Strong, real-feeling moody kitchen shot and a relatable pain-point question. The subline is small at phone size and sits close to the busy table edge. Overall it is a solid hook. It could be sharper with a more specific promise or a number, since the line 'not willpower, a doctor' is the real hook and is buried in the small text.

The real product is clearly shown: the a.clinic site on a phone with the 'Chudnutie, spravené správne' screen. The flat floating phone mockup over a blurred background reads as a template rather than an in-hand creator shot. The on-screen small print is unreadable, but that is acceptable. The headline and fact copy are legible.

The cozy evening living room feels authentic, and the dark gradient makes the text readable. The headline wraps badly, leaving 'nejde' orphaned on its own line. The body leaves 'Slovensku.' orphaned. The laptop screen is not visible, so there is a missed chance to show the questionnaire or video consult.

A believable pharmacy street shot that supports the 'pay at the pharmacy' line. However, the headline is about price transparency, and nothing in the image communicates seeing the price upfront. The visual-to-message link is weak. The text is readable thanks to the gradient.

Awkward framing with the top of the head cropped off and bare feet in the bottom area. The headline sits over a light beige outfit and relies heavily on the shadow. The image does not clearly read as a care team checking in; it could just be any phone call.

final.notes: The gate passes: the a.clinic site on a phone is visible on slide 2, and the last slide carries the questionnaire CTA naming a.clinic. The myth/fact structure is clear and the photography mostly feels native. The biggest fixes are on slide 6: remove the placeholder blue circle, move the text off the face, and make the CTA a clear URL action such as 'Dotazník na a.clinic'. Elsewhere, fix the orphaned words on slides 3 and 6 and reframe slide 5. Consider tying slide 4's visual to upfront pricing, for example a phone showing a price summary. The slide 1 hook would be stronger if the doctor angle were in the headline itself.

slides.issues: Strong, believable kitchen photo with natural light and a real-looking face. Headline is large and readable, and the blue 'diéty' accent works. The body line is small and sits close to the bottom edge, so it is easy to miss at phone size. The hook is relatable but generic; a sharper tension line or number would stop more thumbs.

The real product is visible here: the a.clinic site on a phone, which is good. The blurred background is flat and slightly template-like. On-screen UI copy is tiny at feed size. The site shows '20 minút' while slide 6 says 'asi 10 minút'. This inconsistency undermines trust, so align the numbers. The hero photo on the site reads a bit stock.

Cozy, authentic evening living-room scene. The headline wraps badly and leaves 'nejde' orphaned on its own line. The body also orphans 'Slovensku.' Tighten the line breaks or reduce the font size slightly. The laptop screen is blank, which is a missed chance to show the questionnaire.

The pharmacy storefront with the green cross fits the ePrescription story and feels local and real. The blue highlight includes the comma in 'stojí,', which looks sloppy. Pricing is the strongest objection, but no actual price or example is shown, so the claim feels vague.

Natural candid phone-call shot that reads like real life. The top of her head is cropped tight against the frame edge. The text block covers most of her body, but the gradient keeps it readable. The message is fine but the least punchy myth in the set.

A solid blue circle sits directly over the woman's face, which looks like a placeholder or rendering error. The blue 'dotazníkom' with a glow has weak contrast against the light background. The headline sits on top of her face area, and the photo has a generic AI or stock feel. The CTA pill is clear, but this slide needs a clean image with open space at the top. Ideally it should also show the a.clinic questionnaire on the phone.
